title: Shutdown transport IDs are cleaned up through the wrong event emitter
test: tests/socketTransportShutdownIds.test.js (new; real mediasoup 3.27.1 worker and router, DirectTransports, real socket.io server): 'a receive transport closed when its viewer leaves is dropped from the ignore list', 'receive transports replaced by a new one or closed on disconnect are dropped from the ignore list', 'a host send transport replaced by create-send-transport is dropped from the ignore list', 'destroying a room drops its host and viewer transports from the ignore list', 'transports already closed by their router are not added to the ignore list when the room is destroyed', plus the contract test 'mediasoup reports a closed transport on its observer, not on the transport'
proof: Holds, on the original code too: lib/socket.js at ac1c688 (lines 1115-1134) has the same listener, with mediasoup ^3.27.1. markTransportForShutdown adds the id (lib/socket.js:420) and attachTransportStateHandlers drops it only on transport.on('close') (:1152). mediasoup never emits 'close' on a transport: node_modules/mediasoup/node/lib/Transport.js close() emits '@close' and observer 'close' (:177-179), routerClosed() 'routerclose' and observer 'close' (:213-215), listenServerClosed() 'listenserverclose' and observer 'close' (:253-255). A scratch probe with a real worker printed: WebRtcTransport close() events=["observer:close"], DirectTransport close() events=["observer:close"], router.close() events=["transport:routerclose","observer:close"]. So every socket transport the server closed itself (viewer leave or disconnect, recv transport replaced, host send transport replaced, room destroyed) stayed in the process-wide set until stopJoinCleanup, which runs at startup and in cleanupGlobalResources at shutdown (server.js:1217). On the unchanged code 5 of the 6 new tests failed with 'expected: 0, actual: 1' (leave, replace/disconnect, host replace) and 'expected: 0, actual: 2' (room destroy, router closed first). The existing ignore-list assertions in tests/socketHostSendPath.test.js and tests/socketRecvTransportDeparture.test.js passed only because their fake transports emitted 'close' on themselves, which mediasoup does not. Fix: listen on transport.observer 'close', and skip marking a transport that is already closed (after a router or WebRtcServer close no event follows, so its id would stay). The two fixtures now emit close through an observer as mediasoup does: on the unchanged lib/socket.js 9 of their 17 tests then fail (actual 1), with the fix all pass. Severity is overstated: the ids are random UUIDs that are never reused, so a stale entry changes no behaviour; the cost is memory, about 0.5 KB per id (measured: 100k crypto.randomUUID() strings in a Set on Node 22.14) per transport the server closes, for the life of the process. Checks: touched and related socket test files 39/39; npm run lint and npm run typecheck pass; npm test 999/1000, the one failure tests/portResolver.test.js 'findAvailablePort skips occupied and reserved ports' (ERR_SOCKET_BAD_PORT 65536: the port-0 listener got a port at the top of the range), unrelated, passed 3/3 alone.
